messages.content: Write a plain-language supplement of at most 75 words. Use one sentence per delivered annex, in its given order. For Russia, preserve its objection to an automatic climate-security link and its preferred treatment of the Sahel. For India, explain what it sought to preserve about the climate forum and identify the narrower alternative it supported. For China, preserve its stated limits on climate-security analysis and its principle for allocating climate responsibilities. If both the Russian and Indian explanations are delivered, add one sentence stating what they shared about the UNFCCC and the Sahel alternative. If either annex is absent, make no statement about that delegation's rationale or a shared concern. Keep each explanation attributable to its owner. Use the public record only for procedural context. Avoid restating the public record, attaching legal status to the failed draft, or describing whether evidence was supplied. Output only the requested sentences.

{"fixed_public_record": "On 13 December 2021 at meeting S/PV.8926, the Security Council voted on draft S/2021/990, introduced by Ireland and Niger with other sponsors. It proposed making climate-related security risks a central part of United Nations conflict prevention. The vote was 12 in favour, two against and one abstention. India and Russia opposed it and China abstained. Russia's negative vote as a permanent member prevented adoption. The draft created no new Council authority or requirements.", "annexes_delivered": {"russia-explanation": "Russia opposed the draft's generic, automatic link between climate change and security. It preferred substantive climate work through specialist forums, principally the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC), and an alternative draft addressing the Sahel's specific circumstances and multiple sources of insecurity."}}
